verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents Shared drives as network storage reachable from multiple machines on a private network, and Notebooks come with shared persistent storage. Together these cover the core idea of network-attached storage separate from any single instance. The evidence never says that shared drive data survives machine deletion or how to attach drives to new GPU rentals, and the machine-level 'persistent storage' is a per-machine disk, not network storage. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that shared drives outlive machine teardown, attach/mount workflow details, capacity and performance limits, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Shared drives provide storage that is accessible from multiple machines in a private network.
Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration
